purpose: Native measurements of four authenticated-map constructions under five hash profiles and in-circuit measurements of the three tree candidates under two sponge profiles, against the keyed State contract of specs/sumeragi.md section 16. Input of the G.3 selection.
selection_note: No construction or hash is selected here. G.3 selects, freezes the semantic profile and repeats the final measurements on it.

source.replacement: TODO(G.3): the prototypes, their adapters and this measurement target are deleted when the selected construction is implemented by its State owner; none survives as a second implementation.

constructions.summary: Path-compressed binary radix (crit-bit) Merkle tree over an order-preserving, prefix-free bit encoding of the composite key. Leaves are in canonical key order; the shape depends on the key set alone.
constructions.inclusion: Branching bit index and sibling digest per branch on the leaf's path; sides are key bits.
constructions.absence: The path the absent key's bits select and the disclosed leaf it ends at. One path.
constructions.complete_range: Postfix witness of the covering subtrees: hidden subtrees need a disclosed leaf on their side, none is hidden between revealed leaves.
constructions.update: One compression per distinct branch on the touched paths (dirty marking, one rehash pass).
constructions.depth: About log2(n) for scattered keys plus about log2 of the table count, because the table position heads the composite key; at most 9*len+1 for adversarial keys of len bytes.

constructions.summary: Canonical sorted Merkle B-tree whose page boundaries are chosen by the key digests (a key ends a page of level l when its digest has l+1 leading zero nibbles; sixteen items per page on average). Pages are Merkle-hashed as binary subtrees, so the structure is one binary tree over the sorted leaves.
constructions.inclusion: Side and sibling digest per binary node on the leaf's path.
constructions.absence: The empty complete range [key, key || 0x00): the two adjacent leaves, disclosed.
constructions.complete_range: The same postfix witness as the radix tree, without branching indices.
constructions.update: Every page on the path of a touched key is rehashed (about fifteen compressions per level); a key that newly ends a page also rehashes the following page. The prototype recomputes page-internal nodes; as_built_alternatives projects the cost with those nodes kept.
constructions.depth: About log2(n) plus the imbalance of geometric page sizes. Page sizes are unbounded: chosen keys can grind long pages.

constructions.summary: Indexed linked-leaf Merkle map: every leaf binds its key digest, its value digest and the key digest of the next key in canonical order, between a lower and an upper sentinel. Leaves live in a compressed sparse Merkle tree addressed by key digest, so positions depend on keys alone.
constructions.inclusion: The successor's key digest and the leaf's address path.
constructions.absence: The leaf whose key and successor bracket the absent key, both disclosed. One path, no key-bit selection.
constructions.complete_range: The bracketing leaf below the interval, one address path per claimed entry and the disclosed successor of the last; each successor digest is the next claimed key. The prototype witness carries every path whole; as_built_alternatives counts what paths that share their common nodes would carry.
constructions.update: An insertion or removal rewrites two leaves, a value update one; the sorted neighbour index is not authenticated.

constructions.summary: Baseline: the entries in canonical order folded into one running digest. No tree. It shows what the tree candidates buy; it is not a proposal.
constructions.inclusion: The accumulator before the entry and the leaf digest of every later entry.
constructions.complete_range: The accumulator before the disclosed predecessor, the predecessor and successor leaves and every later leaf digest.
constructions.update: Linear: every accumulator after the first changed position.
constructions.in_circuit: not_shortlisted: every statement is linear in the population

hash_profiles.parameters: BLAKE2b with 256-bit output through iroha_crypto::blake2; all 256 bits kept, no iroha_crypto::Hash marker bit.
hash_profiles.framing: hash_bytes = B(0x00 || le64(domain) || le64(len) || bytes); compress = B(0x01 || le64(domain) || le64(aux) || left || right).
hash_profiles.known_answer_test_reason: The primitive is the repository's existing BLAKE2b owner; the prototype adds framing only.

hash_profiles.parameters: BLAKE3 with 256-bit output. Supplied by the two consumer crates that own a blake3 dependency (the proof crate has none): the conformance adapters and the measurement target each define it, and each checks it against blake3::hash. The framing is the same ByteProfile.

Poseidon2 over Goldilocks, width 12, x^7, 8 full and 22 partial rounds, external matrix circ(2*M4, M4, M4), internal matrix J + diag(d) with the published diagonal. Sponge: capacity 4, rate 8, 4-element digest.
hash_profiles.published_source: Grassi, Khovratovich, Schofnegger, 'Poseidon2: A Faster Version of the Poseidon Hash Function' (2023); Goldilocks width-12 instance of the reference implementation. Round constants are regenerated with the published Grain LFSR procedure and pinned by digest.
hash_profiles.security_note: Published round counts; no security claim is made or checked here (task H.1).

hash_profiles.parameters: Rescue-Prime Rp64_256 over Goldilocks, width 12, x^7 and its inverse, seven rounds, circulant MDS with first row 7,23,8,26,13,10,9,7,6,22,21,8. Sponge: capacity 4, rate 8, 4-element digest.
hash_profiles.published_source: Szepieniec, Ashur, Dhooghe, 'Rescue-Prime: a Standard Specification (SoK)' (2020), as instantiated by winter-crypto 0.13.1 (Rp64_256), whose permutation known-answer vector is pinned.
hash_profiles.security_note: Published round count; no security claim is made or checked here (task H.1). This is Rescue-Prime, not Rescue-Prime Optimized.

hash_profiles.parameters: The repository's six-lane width-3 Poseidon digest (fastpq_isi::poseidon_digest384), reused unchanged and truncated to four lanes so a node keeps 32 bytes. A measurement device, not a proposed construction.
hash_profiles.known_answer_test_reason: The digest is owned and pinned by fastpq_isi; the prototype calls its public entry point.
hash_profiles.security_note: Each lane is a capacity-one sponge; the security of the lane composition and of any truncation is task H.1's subject.

benchmark_identity.hardware_note: Asserted by the operator of the harness; the observed host facts are recorded beside it.
benchmark_identity.config_note: The last component is the first sixteen digits of prototype_sources.sha256, binding the prototype, adapter and measurement files. The checker rejects a different current digest. This limited file set excludes transitive dependencies and does not establish their build provenance or current qualification.
benchmark_identity.source_dirty_note: The source commit and dirty digest describe the checkout when each run executed, not the executable's complete build inputs. The executable SHA-256 and recorded runtime State schema identify the measured artifact and input. An executable retained from an earlier build can measure a newly exported runtime schema; that does not establish a fresh build with current transitive dependencies.
benchmark_identity.harness: scripts/zk_resource_harness.py run (task E.1); records written by crates/iroha_measurement
benchmark_identity.load_note: The measurement runs executed one at a time, none beside another, on a shared development host that other work was also using; the one-minute load average at the start and end of every record is in its row. Every timed phase was repeated on identical inputs inside its run. A test listed more than once in runs was measured again by the same executable; its rows pool both runs.
benchmark_identity.allocator_note: The measuring executable counts heap bytes in its global allocator (two relaxed atomic updates and one thread-local read per allocation, the same for every candidate).

workloads.maximum_note: Maximum measured population, not a maximum supported State workload. The inventory states no population.
workloads.background: Every cell holds its one entry and every other keyed table four entries, so the commitment spans the whole schema.
workloads.change_sets: 1, 100 and 10,000 changes over several tables: of every ten, seven rewrite an entry of the populated table, one inserts there, one removes there and one rewrites an entry of another table or a cell. A size above half the population is not run. Each repetition replays the same sets on a clone of the same built State.
workloads.ranges: Complete ranges of 0, 1, 16 and 1,024 claimed entries with a committed key on each side; in-circuit also 64.
workloads.seed: 0x473220261005; every workload is a pure function of its parameters (workload.rs)
not_run: chain under poseidon2 at 2^20 and under rescue-prime above 2^10: linear in the population under a sponge profile
digest384 beyond radix at 2^16 and all four constructions at 2^10, with fewer statements and no 10,000-change set: one hash costs several thousand BLAKE2b compressions
more than one cold build under rescue-prime at 2^20 and under digest384 at 2^16: one build takes minutes; those builds are marked replicated: false

units.wall_ns: nanoseconds of wall time of the phase, as recorded by iroha_measurement
units.timing: an object {min, median, max, repetitions}: the stated quantity in each repetition of the phase on identical inputs, in nanoseconds per the stated unit of work. The repetitions of one run ran one after another in one process; a row of a test that was run more than once counts the repetitions of every run (record.replicates, timing_comparability.run_to_run). Their spread is the timing's uncertainty under the recorded load. Thread and process CPU time moved with wall time on this host and are not recorded as a load-independent figure.
units.bytes: bytes of the canonical prototype witness encoding, or of the named structure
units.heap_bytes: bytes this executable's counting allocator saw allocated and not yet freed: requested layout sizes, without the allocator's own bookkeeping. A map's heap is counted on the building thread alone; the peak of a reference build or check is counted over every thread of the process
units.compressions: calls of the two-to-one compression of the hash profile
units.byte_hashes: calls of the byte-string hash of the hash profile
units.permutations: width-12 sponge permutations (width-3 lane permutations for digest384)
units.rows: trace rows after padding to a power of two
units.registers: digests the relation's register file holds: the number the statement's evaluation schedule uses, fixed for the trace
units.peak_rss_bytes: process high-water resident set size when the record's session ended; it never falls within a process, so it does not compare candidates measured one after another
units.unattributed_ppm: root wall time outside every phase, in parts per million of the root; the recorder's limit is 10,000

latency.note: Prototype implementations: the algebraic profiles use the proof crate's reference field arithmetic. hash_bytes_N hashes N bytes under the profile's framing. Each operation was timed five times.

as_built_blake2b_gadget.note: Geometry of one BLAKE2b compression in the sealed q77 relation; the comparator for a byte-hash tree in-circuit. Read from the source constants; not measured by this task.

storage_model.note: Engine::storage(): what a persisted node store would keep per node, with node counts read from the structure the prototype holds and bytes per node declared as constants in each construction's source (MODEL_*_BYTES). A model, not a measurement: nothing is persisted, and the B-tree's figure follows from the modelling choice not to keep page-internal nodes. The heap the prototype's containers really hold is in native.rows[].memory.

formulas.btree: entries * entry_bytes + upper_items * upper_item_bytes, upper_items = structure_digests - 2 * entries
formulas.linked: (entries + 1) * leaf_bytes + entries * branch_bytes; auxiliary: entries * index_entry_bytes

native.note: Compression, byte-hash and permutation counts are deterministic functions of the workload and identical in every repetition (class measured_deterministic_count). Timings are {min, median, max, repetitions} over repetitions on identical inputs. storage_model is an accounting model (see storage_model); memory is the heap of the prototype's containers.
native.memory_note: heap_live_bytes is what the building thread held more after the cold build than before it: the measuring executable's allocator counts, for this figure, the allocations and frees of that thread alone while the build runs, so no other thread's allocation is in it. It is the heap of the prototype's own containers (std BTreeMap nodes, the node arena with its spare capacity, the key bytes the prototype keeps, twice for the radix tree), requested layout sizes without the allocator's bookkeeping, and the same in every build of the same State. The figure is the value a strict majority of the cold builds read, in every run that measured the row; heap_readings says how many builds read it and the lowest and highest reading, so a reading that differed would show there. It measures the prototype's in-memory data structures, not a persisted node store. heap_peak_build_bytes is the most the building thread held more during the build, taken the same way. record.peak_rss_bytes is a process high-water mark and compares nothing.

timing_comparability.rule: For each measured group and timing, two constructions are separated (a<b: a is faster) when the [min, max] intervals of their repetitions do not overlap, and overlapping (a~b) otherwise. A timing that was not replicated separates nothing. Where a test was run more than once (run_to_run), a row pools the repetitions of every run, so its interval spans the runs and their different load. Where a test was run once, its repetitions ran back to back inside one process; a difference that is separated there can still be within what another run would show.
timing_comparability.run_to_run_note: A measurement test that was run more than once, by the same executable at another time: for every timed phase of every workload, the further run's median wall time over the first run's. Every count that is not a time was required to be identical in both runs before the rows were written. The rows of such a test pool the repetitions of both runs (record.replicates names the further run and its load).

in_circuit.note: Geometry and permutation counts are deterministic. statements summarises the program of every statement of the native sample beside the permutations of its native verification; geometry and reference describe the first of them. Times are of the uncommitted reference. Every committed-proof field is null with its reason.
in_circuit.memory_note: reference.build_peak_heap_bytes and check_peak_heap_bytes are the most heap the process held during the reference build or check above what it held before, from the counting allocator: the memory of the uncommitted reference for that trace, not prover memory of a committed proof. declared_payload_bytes is the reference's own declared simultaneous payload.
in_circuit.committed_proof_null_reason: No committed proof of this relation exists: the committed q77 engine accepts only its sealed relations until task B.2 generalizes it. Trace-cell scaling from the sealed proof is not an estimate of these fields.

relation_scope.relation: One hash-chain relation per sponge permutation, written against fastpq_prover::air::SemanticAir (crates/fastpq_prover/src/state_commitment_prototypes/circuit.rs): one row per permutation round, a register file of R digests, 18 + 4R numerators of degree at most 8, 13 + 4R private and 20 + 2R verifier-known columns besides the permutation's periodic ones.
relation_scope.registers: R is the number of registers the statement's evaluation schedule uses (Program::registers), at least one. It is fixed for one trace and is part of the relation's identity, width and statement bytes. A deployed relation would fix one R; the figure recorded per statement is what that statement needs.
constrained_in_relation: every permutation round of every hash the native verifier computes, each exactly once: the sponge over the key and value bytes of the statement, the leaf compression, every branch of an opened range tree and the root normalisation
the chaining of each digest into the next permutation, with the side of the previous digest, and the digest a register holds from the block that saved it to the compression that reads it
the statement (key and value blocks), the schema digest and the root, as verifier-known columns and constants

every side that the statement fixes: the bits of the absent key at the disclosed branching indices, every side of an opened range tree (adjacency of the revealed leaves is read from them) and the leaf and link compressions
the successor of every linked leaf of an absence or range statement, as the digest of the disclosed or claimed successor key hashed in the same trace
relation_scope.hash_count: For every statement of the native sample the program's permutation count equals the native verifier's, plus one root normalisation for each anchored chain after the first. Only the linked-leaf range has more than one: it anchors the chain of every leaf where its native verifier compares structure roots and normalises once.
outside_the_relation: Structural checks without a hash (key order against a disclosed neighbour, the shape rules of a range witness) run on verifier-known values when the program is derived, and the skeleton they read (disclosed keys, branching bit indices, statement-fixed sides) is public.

A relation that hides the key, as a State read inside a private execution proof needs, must make the key words private and constrain them. The two gadgets that takes (in_circuit.gadgets) are built and checked as relations of their own; they are not composed into the hash-chain trace. Binding the gadget's limbs to the sponge's message words, hiding the branching indices behind private selectors and constraining the range shape rules remain open for the selected construction (G.3, B.2).
relation_scope.proof_system: Uncommitted algebraic reference of task B.1 (air::build_reference / check_reference): the complete trace in the clear, no commitment, masking, FRI or transcript. Its time and memory are not committed-proof figures.
relation_scope.forgery_tests: crates/fastpq_prover/src/state_commitment_prototypes/circuit_tests.rs. Inclusion: forged siblings, roots and statements are rejected (radix). Absence and complete range, for each of radix, B-tree and linked-leaf under both permutations, through absence_program and range_program: a radix prover following another leaf's path for a committed key, a B-tree absence and a radix or B-tree range that hide a committed entry on the wrong side of its neighbour, a linked leaf whose successor is not the next claimed key; each is rejected by the relation and accepted only without the binding it violates. Each of the eight constraint groups is shown load-bearing by a forged trace that only the relation without that group accepts. The native completeness rules of the range witness have their own crafted-witness tests in fringe.rs.

gadget_scope.relations: crates/fastpq_prover/src/state_commitment_prototypes/key_gadgets.rs: KeyOrderAir (byte-string order, one byte per row, 32 private and 10 verifier-known columns, 47 numerators of degree at most 4) and KeyBitAir (stated bits of the order-preserving key encoding, 11 private and 26 verifier-known columns, 25 numerators of degree at most 3). Both tie the scanned bytes to the byte length and seven-byte limbs the sponge absorbs.
gadget_scope.status: Built and checked standalone with the uncommitted reference, with a forged trace per constraint group. Not composed into the hash-chain trace: the limbs and the length are verifier-known columns here and would be the sponge's private message words in a composed trace.
gadget_scope.instances: Declared per construction and statement kind (WitnessPrograms::ABSENCE_GADGETS, RANGE_GADGETS; recorded with every in-circuit row). Inclusion needs none. Radix absence: two bit scans (the absent key at the branching indices and at one index where the disclosed leaf differs; the disclosed leaf at that index). B-tree and linked-leaf absence: two comparisons (predecessor below the key, successor above it). Every complete range: two comparisons (predecessor below the lower bound, upper bound not above the successor).
gadget_scope.combined_cost: Each in-circuit row carries the sum of its hash-chain trace cells and the trace cells of its gadget instances as a projection. It is a sum of separately measured relations, not the cell count of a composed trace, whose width and degree are open.

as_built_alternatives.note: Two prototype shortcuts shape the comparison as much as the constructions do. These rows project each construction without its shortcut, from counts the measurement took; neither alternative is implemented.

linked_range_shared_paths.note: The prototype's linked-leaf range witness carries one whole address path per leaf. If the paths shared their common nodes (a multiproof), a verifier would hash each branch of their union once and the witness would carry only the siblings outside it. Counted from the prototype's own witnesses; shared_witness_bytes_mean charges 32 bytes per carried sibling and 5 per branch.

btree_cached_page_nodes.note: The prototype B-tree recomputes page-internal nodes on every update and keeps none. If every node of the binary tree were kept, a value rewrite would recompute the leaf and one node per level of its path, and the storage model would grow by one 32-byte digest per page-internal node.

projections.revision: The relation uses 32 rows per permutation, not 30: one row for the initial linear layer and one link row that ties the output to the next permutation. It needs no auxiliary S-box columns: with one register, 12 state columns, one side bit and four register columns are private (17), the other columns are verifier-known selectors, round constants and statement words; each further register adds four private and two verifier-known columns. Numerators have degree at most 8 (a selector times x^7).

decision_criteria.status: proposed for G.3; not frozen and not applied here
admissible_measures: Deterministic counts separate candidates: compressions, byte hashes, permutations, witness bytes, rows, registers, gadget instances. They are identical in every repetition and on every machine.

A timing separates two candidates only where timing_comparability lists the pair as separated for that measure: the intervals of their repetitions do not overlap. A pair listed as overlapping differs by less than the observed spread and is not distinguished by time. timing_comparability.run_to_run states how far the medians of a test moved between two runs; a separation taken from one run alone is weaker than one whose intervals span two.
A timing with replicated: false separates nothing: a cold build run fewer than five times, and every reference build or check of a trace above 4,096 rows.
The storage model is an accounting model and the heap figure is of the prototype's containers; neither is a persisted size. Peak RSS compares nothing.

In-circuit rows compare candidates by their permutation counts, which equal the native verifier's, and by the declared gadget instances. The sum with gadget trace cells is a projection of an uncomposed relation.
screening: K1..K12 conformance of the construction under the profile (met by every candidate listed; see conformance).

A written collision and preimage argument for the hash profile at the root's 256 bits, with the cross-witness consistency of sumeragi.md section 16.4 for any construction built from more than one authenticated component (task H.1 for the hash, G.3 for the construction).
Bit-identical roots, witnesses and verdicts across platforms: cross-platform vectors do not exist yet.
Bounded verification: witness bytes and claimed entries bound the work. The B-tree's page sizes and the radix tree's adversarial depth must be capped or charged before either is admissible.

criteria.question: What does one block's change set cost the publication owner?
How large is the authenticated structure beside the State, and how large is retained history per block (changed nodes)?
How many bytes does a transaction carry per statement kind, and what does a validator spend to verify them?
How many permutations, registers and trace cells does each statement kind need, and what do the gadgets of a private key add?
How do adversarial keys change depth, page size and update cost; how much logic must be exactly canonical?
measures: native.rows[] with key_shape shared-prefix-32 and long-128

decision_criteria.sensitivity: G.3 publishes the outcome under each criterion alone and under the proposed weights before it freezes a choice; a candidate that wins only under one weighting is reported as such.
decision_criteria.hybrid_note: A native value hash under an algebraic tree is admissible only if a proof that asserts value bytes also proves the native value hash; an unconstrained digest is not the value.

limits: The populations are declared experimental assumptions. Neither the State inventory nor this task establishes a production bound; 2^20 entries in one table is the maximum measured population, not a supported maximum.

Times were taken on a shared development host under the recorded load, one measurement run at a time, each timed phase repeated on identical inputs. The deterministic counts do not depend on load; wall times do, and their repetition spread is recorded with them. Only the tests listed in timing_comparability.run_to_run were run twice; every other timing comes from one process.
The algebraic profiles run on the proof crate's reference field arithmetic (128-bit reduction, no vector code). Their native latencies are those of this prototype, not of an optimized implementation.
Witness encodings are prototype encodings (32-bit counts, 32-byte digests). G.3 freezes the wire encoding; byte counts here compare constructions, they are not wire sizes.
No committed proof of the witness relation exists (task B.2). Reference build and check times are for an uncommitted, non-hiding artifact.

The witness relation reads a verifier-known skeleton. The key gadgets of a private key are built and measured on their own and are not composed into the trace; no figure here is the cost of a complete private-key witness relation.
x86-64, device and accelerator measurements were not made. Historical-version storage, pruning, crash recovery and publication are G.3 and G.4 subjects and are not measured.
Rescue-Prime Optimized, Monolith, Tip5 and Anemoi are not implemented; their entries are projections.
